note: The wing-picker. Six questions, each answer gives points to styles. The scoring runs in the reader's own browser. The result links to the style's page; it is a game, not a verdict.
title: Which wing are you?
lede: Six questions. A city hands you a plate at the end. Argue with it — that's the whole point of wings.

a.t: orange, thin, cayenne and melted butter — it runs off the wing
not sauce at all. Seasoning. Dry.
sweet, sticky, red, and it should stain your fingers
hot enough to hurt, and I mean it
blue cheese. Chunky. This is not up for discussion.
ranch, and Buffalo can fight me
white barbecue sauce — mayonnaise, vinegar, black pepper
no dip. The sauce is the dip.
naked. Fried bare, twice if it needs it.
breaded, and fried until it crunches
shatter-crisp, however you got there
smoked first, then whatever finishes it
celery and carrot sticks, on the plate, being ignored
french fries, and the sauce goes over all of it
fried rice, from the same counter
white bread and pickles
flats. Every time. More skin, more sauce.
drums. I want a handle.
whole wing, tip and all, one piece
party wings, a big greasy pile, no counting

questions.q: The seasoning shaker on the table says…

a.t: OLD BAY
lemon pepper
garlic and parmesan, and the pizzeria made it
nothing. There is a bottle of cayenne pepper sauce instead.

buffalo.title: Buffalo
buffalo.say: Cayenne and butter, fried bare, blue cheese, celery you will not eat. You say wings, never Buffalo wings, and you know what year it is supposed to have started.

rochester-breaded.title: Rochester
rochester-breaded.say: Breaded, crunchy, seventy miles east of the argument and winning it locally. Half-and-half if you cannot decide, and a plate under it if you are serious.

atlanta-lemon-pepper.title: Atlanta
atlanta-lemon-pepper.say: Lemon pepper, and the only real question is wet or dry. Fried rice on the side, from the same counter, in the same bag.

chicago-mild-sauce.title: Chicago
chicago-mild-sauce.say: Fried hard, mild sauce over the whole thing, fries underneath soaking it up. The South Side settled this and did not ask anyone.

dc-mumbo.title: Washington, D.C.
dc-mumbo.say: Mumbo sauce, out a carryout window, on wings and fries together. Sweet, red, and named in an argument that reaches Chicago.

baltimore-old-bay.title: Baltimore
baltimore-old-bay.say: Old Bay. On the wings, on the fries, on the rim of the glass. Maryland put it on a crab first and never stopped.

nashville-hot.title: Nashville
nashville-hot.say: Cayenne paste in frying fat, white bread underneath to catch it, pickles on top to survive it. You have made your peace with consequences.

memphis-dry-rub.title: Memphis
memphis-dry-rub.say: Dry. Rubbed before, dusted after, off the same counter as the ribs. A wet wing is a different order and you will not be making it.

korean-american.title: Korean America
korean-american.say: Fried twice, crust like glass, sweet-hot glaze, pickled radish to reset the mouth. You order the whole wing and eat the tip.

caribbean-jerk.title: Jerk
caribbean-jerk.say: Allspice, thyme and scotch bonnet, marinated overnight, over fire rather than in oil. Brooklyn, the Bronx, Miami, Hartford — pick your block.

alabama-white.title: Alabama white
alabama-white.say: Mayonnaise, vinegar, a lot of black pepper, and a smoked wing dunked straight into it. North Alabama has been doing this since 1925 and rarely mentions it.

smoked-bbq-wing.title: The barbecue joint
smoked-bbq-wing.say: Whole wings on the smoker beside the brisket. Slower than a fryer, and the skin is the part you argue about.

garlic-parm.title: Garlic parmesan
garlic-parm.say: Butter, garlic, a snowfall of cheese, no pepper anywhere. The pizzeria's answer, and now half the country's.
